title: Fixed Cam-Lift Two-Stamp Ore Mill
description: One newly authored complete static historical ore-stamp appearance: a grounded twin-post frame carries a horizontal camshaft, two distinct fixed flat-crest cam/tappet contacts, two whole square stamp stems passing through actual square bores in two closed guide bodies, raised heads and one genuinely open blind-bottom mortar. A fixed four-spoke rim completes the shaft appearance. The whole cam-to-tappet and guided falling-stem arrangement is structurally different from the old single-column bench drill, lever citrus press, threaded-spindle basket press and smith scene with hand tools; adding a second head is not the novelty. All main geometry newly authored using mature boxes, annuli, polygon extrusions and a small boundary-cell guide primitive. Both heads remain above the mortar floor, the two cams are fixed in different phases, and the bore spaces occupied by stems/shaft are not claimed fully clear. Static art only: no motor/belt drive, motion cycle, impact force, ore crushing capacity, manufacturing, installation, guarding, structural loading or machinery safety claim.
